sources.title: The Revenue Administration of the Northern Sarkars, 1759 to 1786
sources.note: SOAS thesis on Mughal grant, Nizam treaties, early Company control, revenue institutions and local intermediaries.

sources.title: Reference Tools for Research
sources.note: National Archives of India guide identifies East India Company political and secret records for the period.

sources.title: Colonial acquisition of the Northern Circars
sources.note: Regional historical scholarship on the layered farman, treaties and transfer rather than a one-day conquest.

sources.title: District Survey Report of Koraput
sources.note: Odisha district source for plateaus, rivers, rainfall, forests and present administrative geography; used cautiously for landscape.

sources.title: Nabarangpur District Gazetteer
sources.note: Government gazetteer preserves regional political traditions and the Vizianagaram succession after Padmanabham.

sources.title: Highland Odisha: Life and Society beyond the Coastal World
sources.note: Scholarly collection emphasizes highland diversity, ritual politics and plural authority rather than coastal-state uniformity.

sources.title: The forest and the state in Bastar
sources.note: Anthropological history rejects a timeless opposition between isolated tribes and an all-powerful state.

sources.title: Famine in the Northern Circars, 1791 to 1792
sources.note: Oxford scholarship links crop failure, war, revenue pressure, labor and hunger in the exact coastal region.

sources.title: Vizianagaram under Company rule
sources.note: University repository history of Company revenue demands, disarmament, the 1794 battle and the minor heir’s settlement.

sources.title: Mackenzie Collection: Southern India surveys
sources.note: British Library archive catalogue documents roads, drawings and surveys in the Northern Circars and Deccan.

sources.title: Vizianagaram: loans to the East India Company
sources.note: British Library archive entry shows fiscal relationships between the Company and Vizianagaram estate.

sources.title: Water Architecture in South Asia
sources.note: SOAS research on tanks, wells, stepped access and the social meanings of water structures.

sources.title: The Value of Tanks
sources.note: IIHS study explains maintenance labor, ecology and colonial change in South Indian tank systems.

sources.title: Indian rivers, productive works and large dams in nineteenth-century Madras
sources.note: Historical Journal article supplies later comparison for irrigation and colonial public-works claims.

sources.title: Medicine and the Company in Madras
sources.note: Peer-reviewed history of plural medical markets, military medicine, dispensaries and biased European sanitation observations.

sources.title: Early colonial medical institutions in India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed history notes Indian dressers and doctors employed by Company services in the late eighteenth century.

sources.title: Ayurvedic Man: Encounters with Indian Medicine
sources.note: Wellcome Collection explains historically changing Ayurvedic knowledge and cautions against a single timeless medical system.

sources.title: William Roxburgh botanical illustrations
sources.note: Botanical Survey of India archive for Roxburgh, the Samalkot garden and Plants of the Coast of Coromandel.

sources.title: William Roxburgh and the colonial botanical network
sources.note: University of Edinburgh thesis supplies context for collecting, local knowledge and imperial botanical science.

sources.title: Length of long cloth from the Coromandel Coast
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum object record anchors Coromandel cotton production and global circulation.

sources.title: Interwoven Globe
sources.note: Met exhibition traces worldwide textile trade and the skill and demand attached to Indian cottons.

sources.title: Textile production on the Coromandel Coast
sources.note: Economic history of weavers, merchants and Company intervention in coastal production.

sources.title: Traditional rice and millet knowledge in Odisha
sources.note: Scholarly study of regional crop diversity; used as later comparison rather than an exact 1790 menu.

sources.title: Crop assemblages and food traditions in Odisha
sources.note: Modern scientific comparison demonstrates crop diversity while warning against projecting current recipes backward.

sources.title: Education in eighteenth-century India
sources.note: NCERT journal discusses indigenous schools, teachers, pupils and later colonial evidence limits.

sources.title: Beyond Macaulay: Education in India, 1780 to 1860
sources.note: Scholarly volume frames multilingual education before and during early colonial reorganization.

sources.title: Learned communities in early modern South India
sources.note: University dissertation on teachers, manuscripts, patronage and scholarly networks.

sources.title: Gender, family and work in textile history
sources.note: American Historical Association essay supplies comparative questions about household work and gender without universalizing roles.

sources.title: Household workers of East India Company ports
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Bengal comparison documents servants, dependency and unfree labor in Company port households.

sources.title: Slavery and the Household in Bengal, 1770 to 1880
sources.note: SOAS research demonstrates coercive household labor outside the exact footprint; used as explicit regional comparison.

sources.title: Parliament and the East India Company
sources.note: UK Parliament history explains state oversight, monopoly and the Company’s unusual political character.

sources.title: East India Company parliamentary inquiry papers
sources.note: British Library catalogue anchors parliamentary investigation in surviving primary records.

sources.title: Pitt’s India Act and dual control
sources.note: Cambridge research explains the 1784 Board of Control and divided Company-Crown governance.

sources.title: South Asia, 1600 to 1800 A.D.
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum chronology presents multiple courts, regional powers and artistic traditions.

sources.title: Maratha political history
sources.note: Maharashtra government historical gazetteer for confederate politics rather than a single monolithic Maratha state.

sources.title: Hyderabad history and the 1798 alliance
sources.note: Government research institute volume discusses Nizam rule and the subsidiary alliance.

sources.title: The Sikh Empire and its setting
sources.note: Oxford scholarship distinguishes Sikh misls and Ranjit Singh’s emerging kingdom from later empire.

sources.title: Sikh history timeline
sources.note: Museum timeline anchors Ranjit Singh’s taking of Lahore in 1799; used with scholarly context.

sources.title: Tipu Sultan and the Mysore Wars
sources.note: National Army Museum history of Mysore, Tipu and the 1799 siege.

sources.title: Tipu Sultan’s sons delivered as hostages
sources.note: Museum object record documents the child hostages demanded after the 1792 treaty.

sources.title: An unknown soldier in the Second Mysore War
sources.note: National Army Museum uses a soldier’s words to show hunger, disease and danger behind campaigns.

sources.title: Tipu’s Tiger
sources.note: Victoria and Albert Museum explains the Mysore court’s wooden tiger organ and its sounds.

sources.title: The tiger and the queen
sources.note: V&A provenance essay confronts Company looting after Seringapatam and the museum lives of seized objects.

sources.title: Tipu Sultan papers: Aḥkāmnāmah
sources.note: British Library catalogue dates a Persian manuscript titled Aḥkāmnāmah to Tipu’s court, 1793 to 1798.
